headline: Core industrial growth intact despite a gains-timing dip
summary_short: EastGroup's Q2 revenue rose to $193M (+1.6% q/q, +9.1% y/y) and FFO per diluted share climbed to $2.36 (+6.8% y/y), while net income of $76M fell 20.2% q/q because Q1 included a much larger one-time gain on property sales.
summary_long: Revenue rose to $193M (+1.6% q/q, +9.1% y/y) on 6.2% same-property NOI growth plus new development and 2025-2026 acquisitions. FFO per diluted share climbed to $2.36 (+6.8% y/y) as PNOI growth outpaced higher G&A and interest expense. Net income fell to $76M (-20.2% q/q) because Q1 included a $24.9M property-sale gain versus $5.2M in Q2 - a timing effect; y/y net income rose 19.3%. Occupancy was 95.6% and new/renewal leasing spreads averaged 34.1%. This 10-Q disclosed no forward guidance. Cash rose to $33M; long-term debt held flat q/q at $1,615M.

PNOI increased $7.6M from same-property operations, $3.6M from newly developed/value-add properties and $3.0M from 2025-2026 acquisitions, partly offset by $0.7M from properties sold.
Reflects underlying PNOI and FFO growth; six-month diluted EPS of $3.17 vs $2.35 was also aided by a $30.1M YTD gain on property sales, $24.9M of which landed in Q1.
Q1 booked a $24.9M gain on real estate sales versus just $5.2M in Q2 - the swing in one-time sale gains, not weaker operations, drives the q/q decline.
Company attributes the increase primarily to higher PNOI, partially offset by an increase in general and administrative expense and interest expense.
